_note: Fallback time budgets in minutes, used only when a dispatch brought no `Budget:` line (dispatch-guard.py denies that for these types, so this is a fallback). Only these agent types are budgeted.
_note_dispatch: worker_dispatch_margin_minutes: minutes a headless worker keeps for its wrap-up report; dispatch-guard.py denies a dispatch whose `Budget:` minutes plus this margin exceed the run's minutes left.
_note_phases: worker_max_phases: how many PHASE turns run-worker.sh compacts and resumes in one run (test-first has 2: tests-done, dev-done); a loop guard.
_note_dispatch_usd: worker_dispatch_margin_usd: USD a headless worker keeps for its wrap-up; dispatch-guard.py denies a dispatch whose `Budget:` usd plus this margin exceeds the run's remaining budget_usd.
_note_headroom: budget_headroom: a budget is the estimate of the work (Budget line, plans/worker/<topic>.json); the limits sit this factor above it. subagent-budget.py denies a subagent's tool calls at budget x this; worker-control.py gives a worker run minutes x this (CLAUDE_WORKER_MINUTES, the background wait ceiling) and est_usd x this (--max-budget-usd). The checks that a dispatch fits (dispatch-guard.py) use the estimate itself, so the headroom stays for overruns. Replaces the 80% checkpoint, worker_usd_cap_factor 1.2 and the floors (agent_floor, worker_floor, worker_minutes_floor_ratio), 2026-11-01: a budget equal to the mean need and stopped at 80% of it stopped 17-18 of 33 replayed rounds; at 1.25 x the mean, 4-5. Hook waits (mutation scan, crap-gate coverage) are reserved by cost-history.py and dispatch-guard.py from the recorded waits, not by a floor.
_note_estimate: The estimate model (cost-history.py, 2026-11-01): per agent, per branch class and for merge runs, over the last estimate_window rows with a raw estimate, need = fixed + slope x raw, fixed = the estimate_fixed_quantile of the actuals, slope = the largest (actual - fixed) / raw. No floors (user 2026-11-01: they hid that a single factor scaled small jobs below their fixed part). Chosen by replaying the history (skills/repo-plan/estimate-replay.py): subagents 3 of 96 rounds stopped, worker runs 4 of 32; re-run it before changing these.
_note_auto_resume: Automatic resume (worker-control.py auto, 2026-11-01): when dispatch-guard.py stops a run only because the planned dispatch doesn't fit its time or USD, it records what a resume needs (the dispatch budget, the gate wait, the wrap-up margins, plus worker_resume_startup_minutes/_usd for re-reading the compacted session and the plan). worker-control.py starts at most worker_auto_resume_max such resumes in a row per topic (a wt launch or wt resume by the user resets the count), only when the record's minutes and USD stay within worker_auto_resume_max_minutes / _usd, and never with an ALERT or HOLD pending. The resume's limits sit budget_headroom above the record, as for any run. The resume gets the larger of that record and what is left of the estimate of the last run the user started, capped at worker_auto_resume_max_minutes / _usd (a record covers only the one dispatch that didn't fit). A later dispatch that fits deletes the record. wt-pane's auto mode sends wt resume itself, which resets the count: with it on, worker_auto_resume_max no longer limits anything.
_note_auto_merge: Automatic merge run (local mode, 2026-11-01): when auto-merge.py refuses a STATUS: done run only because the branch lacks the latest main, worker-control.py auto-merge resumes it in merge mode (merge.md) with these minutes and USD as its estimate (limits budget_headroom above), at most worker_auto_merge_max in a row per topic (a wt launch or wt resume by the user resets it). Sized from the one recorded merge run (signal-eval, TODO.md conflict: $1.05, 5.5 min, estimate $1.20, 15 min) plus room for a developer round on an implementation conflict and the merge review.
_note_auto_fix: Automatic fix run (local mode, 2026-11-01): when the real data shows a STATUS: done run wrong (verify.py's failed check, or the verifier's fail; auto-merge.py "fix_run"), worker-control.py auto-fix resumes the worker with the findings, at most worker_auto_fix_max times in a row (a run the person starts resets the count). worker_auto_fix_usd / _minutes: the raw guess for one fix (a qa fixture, a developer fix, one review), which cost-history.py estimate branch --fix corrects with the history of earlier fix runs (agent "fix") and adds one review's and one developer round's gate waits to; it is the starting point of the model, not a limit.
_note_verifier: The verifier (verifier.py, 2026-11-01), the second real-data layer: its budget is the verify spec's raw estimate ("verifier": {"usd", "minutes"}) through the history model of agent "verifier"; subagent-budget.py enforces it like any agent's. verifier_session_usd: added to --max-budget-usd for the headless session around the fork (system prompt, skill, relaying the report). verifier_grace_minutes: added to budget x budget_headroom before verifier.py stops the session, for a command still running when the budget hook stops the agent and for its report; a stop is an error for the person, never a pass.
_note_queue: The topic queue (wt_queue.py, local mode, 2026-11-01): plans the person queued with `wt queue` start one after another, as many at once as these allow. queue_max_workers: busy topics at once (a run going, or an automatic resume or merge run decided). queue_max_concurrent_usd: their estimates (est_usd) summed, the next one's included. Generic defaults: a repo sets its own in .claude/flow.json {"queue": {...}} (read from the local main's commit), and its own resource tags in each plans/queue/<topic>.json.
_note_queue_quota: The subscription's usage limits for the topic queue (wt_queue.py, 2026-11-01): no new start while the 5-hour or weekly window is at these percentages or above (quota-snapshot.py, the status line, writes ~/.claude/quota/usage.json; the status line JSON is the only documented source). A snapshot older than queue_quota_max_age_minutes, or none, is unknown usage: queue_quota_unknown "wait" starts nothing until a session refreshes it, "start" goes on without it. The person's limits, not a repo's: no override in .claude/flow.json. Runs already going are not stopped.
_note_queue_done: queue_done_linger_minutes: how long a queued topic that was merged and finished stays in the queue listing (pane, wt queue) before a tick removes it; its plans/queue files go to the archive when it is marked done.
